output.summary: The yield decline is real: the CMM measurement system is stable (E4) and the FPY definition is unchanged (E2). The new-operator hypothesis is contradicted, because FPY fell before they ran alone and their reject rate matches the experienced operators' (E14). Three causes remain confounded. These are the Corvane hardness spread, spindle wear after the deferred service (L3-02 and L3-05 are over the runout limit), and 12-hour-shift fatigue. Lot sequence, service deferral and shift change all overlap in time, and the defect codes cannot tell them apart (E12). Scrap tag times do not give the hour a part was cut (E3). The backlog pressure to defer service is documented (E9, E16). Reverting shifts, cancelling Corvane, penalizing operators or cutting inspection would each be premature or harmful. The staggered service with trial lots and hour-of-machining recovery (A2) best separates the causes. The Line 6 Corvane CMM results (X6) would also help.
